messages:
sara_support: Customer (AcmeCo) says they were charged twice after re-attaching a PO. Invoices INV-2026-4432 and INV-2026-4433 for the same billing period. They attached the PO after renewal; looks like a stale card auth retriggered a second renewal. Can someone triage and refund?

alex_billing: Acknowledged. I can run a quick check on the payment events. Do we have the transaction IDs?

kate_cs: I have the customer's note and the receipt screenshots. Transaction IDs on their side: txn_7Y8Z3 and txn_7Y8Z3_dup (they're showing two captures for same amount). Uploaded to the ticket.

juna_engineer: Pulling logs for the billing job that processed that account. Hypothesis: webhook retry for PO attach created a second charge because the idempotency key was missing on the backend batch call. Will check sequence IDs.

mike_payments: I see two capture events in payments ledger: capture_20260301_001 and capture_20260301_002 referencing customer_id acme-889. Both were created within 40s of each other. One was initiated by auto-renew job, the other by the PO-attach flow.

sara_support: Repro steps from customer: 1) Auto-renew at 03:02 triggers invoice INV-2026-4432 2) Customer realizes needs PO, attaches PO in UI 03:03 3) They click "submit PO" and get UI confirmation 03:03 4) They see an extra charge a few seconds later.

juna_engineer: Found a webhook payload duplication in the server logs around 2065004323. Looks like the frontend retried the attach call and the attach handler triggered billing without checking if the renewal already completed. Payload snippet:

```json
{"event":"po.attach","customer":"acme-889","po_id":"PO-9087","attempt":2}
```

juna_engineer: The billing handler should be idempotent by invoice id but the attach path calls /billing/charge without idempotency-key header. That explains the double charge.

alex_billing: Thanks. What's the impact? Any refunds pending?

mike_payments: I'll do a manual reversal for the duplicate capture. Issuing refund now against capture_20260301_002. Refund ID RFND-98765. Marking as priority.

ops-bot: Payment reversal RFND-98765 created by mike_payments at 2065004500. Status: processing.

kate_cs: Chatted with the customer, told them we issued a refund and will confirm once it posts. They asked for an ETA on when funds return — can we give them a window?

mike_payments: Typical posting 3-5 business days depending on bank. I'll follow up when processor confirms.

juna_engineer: For the fix: will add idempotency-key enforcement to the PO attach -> billing path and add a pre-check to skip charging if invoice already exists/paid. Also adding a short-term rule to log and alert when two captures for same customer+period occur within 60s.

alex_billing: Can we also add a reconciliation job that flags same-amount same-customer charges within a short window? Would help catch races.

juna_engineer: Yes, adding a high-priority task. I'll open a PR for the idempotency header and the pre-check today.

sara_support: Filing follow-up items in the support ticket: refund issued RFND-98765, engineering fix planned (idempotency + pre-check), reconciliation alert. Notifying finance for any chargebacks.

kate_cs: Customer confirmed receipt of the refund email and appreciates quick action. They'll escalate to their AP if refund not posted in 5 business days.

mike_payments: Refund processed by processor at 2065004550, processor_ref proc_3321. I'll update the ledger once settlement clears.

ops-bot: Reminder: create postmortem in #postmortems within 72 hours for duplicate-billing incidents with customer impact.

sara_support: Closing loop here. Thanks team. Action items: mike -> confirm settlement; juna -> PR + alert; alex -> add reconciliation job; kate -> keep customer updated. :thumbsup:
